description:
FOUND s499k (Opus, 2026-09-27) probing #2443.  PRE-EXISTING (identical on main 937e7b65).

Reproducer (perl 5.40.3 vs PCL):
    my $p = q(^\Qa.b\E$);
    print "a.b" =~ /$p/ ? 1 : 0, "|", "Qa.bE" =~ /$p/ ? 1 : 0, "\n";   # perl 0|1   PCL 1|0

CAUSE: `\Q…\E` is a DOUBLE-QUOTED-string operator, applied when a pattern LITERAL is interpolated (toke.c); in pattern TEXT that reaches the regex compiler at run time (a variable holding a backslash-Q), `\Q` is an unrecognised escape, the letter Q.  perl-regex-to-ppcre applies quotemeta to `\Q…\E` in EVERY pattern it translates, runtime ones included.  Silent wrong, rare (a pattern read from data or built in single quotes).

FIX SHAPE (not tried): the compiler already knows which \Q belongs to the literal; the runtime pass should only see \Q that came from a literal — e.g. the literal path applies it at transpile time (as the dq decoder does, ir-spec §3.2g) and the runtime pass is deleted, or the runtime pass is told the pattern is interpolated/literal.  Probe `qr/\Q$x\E/` (must still quote $x's value), `m/\Qa.b/`, a pattern from a variable, split and s///.
subject: SILENT WRONG (pre-existing, rare): \Q...\E in RUNTIME pattern text is applied as quotemeta; perl reads it as the letter Q (it is a dq-string operator, not a regex one)
